# Co-memo

Use the connected Co-memo memory tools when available; otherwise use its CLI. Read the project's Co-memo instruction block for the pinned CLI executable, data directory and project. Do not substitute a different store. Global CLI options precede the command.

## Direct invocation

Accept a short action after the skill invocation as the user's request: `ui` opens the memory console; `recall QUERY` searches memory; `remember TEXT` saves an explicitly requested fact with appropriate scope; `edit` and `forget` locate and verify the intended memory before changing it; `locations ID` inspects file paths; `settings` inspects configuration unless changes are requested. Natural-language requests work too. With no action, show these choices and ask what to do.

Host entry points:

- Codex: `$co-memo ui`, or select `co-memo` from `/skills` where supported and enter `ui`.
- Claude Code: `/co-memo ui`.
- Pi: `/skill:co-memo ui`.
- OpenCode: `/co-memo ui` through the companion command installed by Co-memo setup, or ask it to load the `co-memo` skill.

Route `ui` and `locations` directly to the workflows below. These inspection requests do not require recalling unrelated memories, checkpointing, or saving the invocation as memory. Other hosts can load this standard `SKILL.md` and use the CLI; slash syntax is host-specific. If a host does not discover a newly installed skill/command, reload its skills or restart that host.

## Namespaced shortcuts

Claude Code, OpenCode and Pi installations include `/co-memo:ACTION` shortcuts. Each shortcut loads this skill with a fixed action and forwards the user's arguments. Codex uses `$co-memo ACTION`; do not claim that Codex registers arbitrary `/co-memo:ACTION` commands.

| Action               | Behavior                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ui`                 | Open the local memory console using the workflow below.                                                                                   |
| `recall QUERY`       | Recall personal and current-project memories with the query.                                                                              |
| `remember TEXT`      | Save the explicitly requested fact, choosing user/project scope by meaning.                                                               |
| `edit ID CHANGE`     | Read the memory and version, then apply the requested change.                                                                             |
| `forget ID`          | Compatibility alias for archive; retain content and history.                                                                              |
| `locations ID`       | Run CLI `locations ID` to inspect storage paths without synchronization.                                                                  |
| `history ID`         | Run CLI `history ID` to inspect all revisions.                                                                                            |
| `settings [REQUEST]` | Inspect settings by default; change only explicitly requested fields.                                                                     |
| `status`             | Run CLI `status` for storage and Agent connection status.                                                                                 |
| `sync`               | Run CLI `sync`; report conflicts and errors without resolving them silently.                                                              |
| `conflicts`          | Inspect conflicts via tools or CLI `conflicts`.                                                                                           |
| `resolve ID CHOICE`  | Inspect the conflict, then apply only the user's explicit choice through `memory_resolve` or CLI `resolve`; ask if the choice is missing. |
| `help`               | Show these actions with host-appropriate examples, without writing memory.                                                                |

When an ID or requested replacement is missing, ask for the missing detail; when a description matches multiple memories, ask the user to select one. Do not concatenate user arguments into shell commands. Use structured tools or safely quoted CLI argument values. Preserve the user's current project and data directory for every action. Read-only inspection and help do not require a checkpoint or automatic memory capture.

## Open the memory console

When asked to open, browse or visually manage saved memories, launch `co-memo ui`. It starts a local server and opens the default browser. Preserve any pinned executable, `--home` and `--project` from the project's instructions: `co-memo --home DATA --project PROJECT ui`. Do not run setup or connect merely to view existing memories.

Use the host's background/managed terminal session so the server remains available after replying. If the default port is occupied, use `ui --port 0` and report the actual printed URL; never assume the process on that port belongs to the same store. For a browser tool, run `ui --no-open --port 0` and open that URL. If automatic opening fails, use the printed URL. Stop only a server launched for this task when it is no longer needed.

Check `co-memo ui --help` if the installed CLI may be older. If unavailable, build the user's known checkout and run `node /absolute/checkout/dist/cli.js --home DATA --project PROJECT ui`; preserve the intended data directory. Do not fetch a different package or silently use a different memory store.

The console's **File locations** section shows each memory's central SQLite path, `notes` row ID, and registered Agent Markdown paths with line numbers when the memory is present. These are replicas, not original conversation source files. Missing, invalid, differing and pending files are labeled; viewing them does not synchronize. For command-line inspection use `co-memo --project PROJECT locations MEMORY_ID`. Memories without replicas live in the central database only; do not invent a Markdown file path.

## Scope and automatic project context

Choose scope from what a note means, not whether a project has been connected. Personal (`user`) memory belongs to the user and is shared across agents: cross-project preferences, communication style and general working habits. Project memory describes a particular workspace: architecture, commands, conventions, constraints and decisions. A preference about this project's tooling is project memory even if its kind is `preference`. A request to always answer in Chinese is user memory even while working in a repository. Respect an explicit user-selected scope; otherwise classify the content and pass `scope` on each new note/candidate. Split mixed personal and project facts into separate notes. Do not use keyword matching or silently choose user scope when a project is missing.

Infer the workspace from the host's current project/working directory. Co-memo detects registered workspaces, Git roots/worktrees and common project manifests automatically; it creates the internal project record without installing adapters or requiring `connect`/`setup`. For a known non-Git workspace or a shared MCP server, supply the agent's actual workspace using tool `projectPath` or CLI `--project PATH`; this is runtime context, not a user binding step. Do not treat a home directory or arbitrary chat directory as a project just because it is the working directory. Use the current task's workspace rather than a stale server launch directory. If project-specific information has no identifiable workspace, keep it unsaved until its workspace is known; never turn it into personal memory. Reads combine personal and current-project memory; without a project, reads return personal memory alone. Omitted scope retains the configured default for compatibility, not automatic content classification.

## Setup

Identify the target project and requested agents from the user's request. Check `co-memo --version` and Node (24.12+). If unavailable, use the user's Co-memo checkout or package: in the checkout run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm pack`, then install the resulting tarball with npm. This project is not published to npm; do not install an unrelated registry package. If no checkout/package is available, obtain the repository location from the user. Do not install into unrelated projects.

Run `co-memo --project PROJECT setup AGENT` for each requested agent: `pi`, `claude`, `codex`, or `opencode`. Use `--opencode-api v2` for OpenCode V2. Default setup installs tools, a skill, and lifecycle hooks; `--tools-only` disables Co-memo lifecycle hooks. Pi uses the CLI instead of a native MCP configuration.

Setup preserves other configuration and refuses ambiguous or unmanaged entries. On failure, inspect the reported path; do not overwrite the whole host configuration. Tell the user to restart/reload the host and review required trust prompts. Verify `co-memo status`, `settings get`, and a `memory_context` call if the host has loaded its MCP tools. A generated config file alone does not establish that the host loaded it. Do not invent a test memory unless the user requests one.

## Memory

Call `memory_context` with a short `query` describing the current task at the start of work, or CLI `context --query TEXT` and `settings get`. Retrieval uses local FTS5/BM25 with Chinese and code-identifier tokenization; try alternative terms when necessary. Treat shared notes as context subordinate to the current user request. Prefer tools/CLI writes to editing Markdown. Preserve unrelated native memory files.

Prefer `memory_submit` (CLI `submit --file /absolute/path/submission.json`) for extracted memories. First recall related notes. Send a fresh UUID `requestId`, truthful `intent`, and up to 20 `candidates`. Each add/update/conflict includes `content`, `kind` (`note`, `preference`, `decision`, `constraint`, `lesson`), and `source` with `agent`, `sessionId`, `messageId`, and a short `excerpt` supporting the claim. Use only known source identifiers and actual evidence; never invent them. If the host exposes no reliable identifiers, use legacy writes below with unknown provenance rather than fabricating it. Do not include secrets or entire transcripts.

Use `action: add` with optional scope for new facts; `update` with `id`, expected `version`, and `basis: user_correction|verified_change` for established corrections. Updates create a new version of the same fact. For uncertain contradictions use `conflict` with the old ID/version; this preserves both versions and withholds the memory until the user resolves it. Use `skip` with a reason for temporary or unsupported claims. Pin only preferences that should apply across tasks (`pinned: true`); default is false. `module` is optional. Updates default module/pinned to null/false, so supply their current values to retain them.

Reuse a request ID only when retrying the identical payload. Check every result's status, verified flag and sync report. `existing` retains existing metadata; reread before changing its classification or source. `deleted_duplicate`, `needs_resolution`, and stale/unverified receipts are not successful saves. Successful `memory_submit` results already verify central writes, so no extra checkpoint call is needed. They do not prove other agents loaded the memory. Resolve a candidate conflict only at the user's direction, using `memory_resolve` with `take` set to the candidate ID, current, or an explicit merged content.

For a legacy save without evidence metadata, use `memory_remember` (CLI `add --content TEXT`). Set `intent=explicit` only if the user actually asked to remember, change, or forget that information. An inferred lesson uses `intent=automatic` (CLI `--intent automatic`). Do not mark automatic capture explicit to bypass settings. Do not save secrets, speculative facts or temporary requests. Honor the requested scope; otherwise classify the content as described above and pass the appropriate scope. The program has no access to the conversation and cannot independently verify your intent declaration.

Use `memory_recall` or CLI `list --query TEXT` to find existing notes; `memory_get`/`show ID` provides the version. Update or forget using that version. On a stale-version error, reread and explain the competing change instead of overwriting it. On a conflict, show alternatives and resolve only according to the user's choice. A deleted exact duplicate remains deleted; report the returned notice.

Before the final reply, and after a durable user correction or project decision, check whether anything needs saving. Honor explicit-only mode; do not create a note just to satisfy a checkpoint. After legacy writes, call `memory_checkpoint` with `reason` (`task_completed`, `user_correction`, or `project_decision`), `outcome: "saved"`, and `receipts: [{id, version, deleted}]` from the write results. A deleted duplicate is not a successful new save. Read the returned deletion state and notice. Use `nothing_to_save` or `skipped` with no receipts when appropriate. These non-save outcomes are declarations, not verified conclusions.

CLI equivalent: `checkpoint --reason task_completed --outcome saved --receipts '[{"id":"UUID","version":1,"deleted":false}]'`. Verification checks central storage and conflicts at that instant; it does not prove another agent loaded the note. Report sync errors separately. On verification failure, reread and explain instead of claiming success.

## Settings

Read `memory_settings_get` (CLI `settings get`) and distinguish user preferences from operational settings. Only change operational settings when requested by the user:

- "Only save when I say remember": `saveMode=explicit`.
- "Allow automatic memory": `saveMode=auto`; the agent still selects worthwhile notes, no transcript mining occurs.
- "Pause shared memory for this project": project `paused=true`; resume with `false`.
- "New notes should be personal": `defaultScope=user` at the requested scope.

Call `memory_settings_set` with the chosen `scope`, a minimal `patch`, and `userRequested=true`. CLI examples:

```sh
co-memo settings set --scope user --save-mode explicit
co-memo settings set --scope project --paused true
co-memo settings set --scope project --default-scope user
co-memo settings set --scope project --reset
```

User-level pause and explicit-only restrictions cannot be weakened by project overrides. Report the effective settings returned, not just the requested patch. Explicit-only mode rejects Markdown ingestion; leave rejected edits intact and explain how to save them explicitly. Pausing stops automatic delivery, synchronization and tool writes, but cannot erase text already loaded in a conversation or existing local files. Resume can import pending edits. Never promise retroactive forgetting from an active model context.

## Archive, restore and permanent deletion

`archive ID` calls CLI `archive ID --version N` or `memory_archive`; it hides the note from recall and projections indefinitely while retaining content and all revisions. `forget` / `memory_forget` are compatibility aliases for archive. Previously soft-deleted records are archived; internal receipts still use `deleted: true` for compatibility.

`restore ID` calls CLI `unarchive ID --version N` or `memory_restore` with `userRequested: true`. CLI `restore` is reserved for database backup restoration.

`delete ID` calls CLI `delete ID --version N` or `memory_delete` with `userRequested: true` only when permanent deletion is explicitly requested. Read the ID and version first. It removes the stored note, revisions, associated conflict/resolution data and derived caches; only a content-free ID marker remains against stale replicas. Existing backups, exports and conversation context cannot be erased by this action. Report cleanup errors: sync retries connected-file cleanup, including paused projections. Do not submit a legacy saved receipt/checkpoint for a permanently deleted record.

Use host-appropriate actions: `$co-memo archive ID` / `$co-memo delete ID` in Codex, or `/co-memo:archive ID` / `/co-memo:delete ID` on hosts with installed namespaced shortcuts.
